role.altitude: The editor keeps shaping the story, building effects, working with the director and departments and reading scripts; checking time codes against paper reports, syncing by hand and preparing turnovers shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting up ingest checks and export presets with the set and departments
role.ambitious_version: An editor who starts cutting on the morning after the shoot because media arrive checked and synced.

tasks.short: Have digital camera and sound reports filled on set, receive the media, verify key numbers and time codes on materials against the reports, sync sound and picture, chase discrepancies and check time codes in the edit list before delivery.

steps.what: Camera assistant and sound recordist fill in the camera and sound reports on set
Film editor receives the camera media and sound files with the reports
Film editor verifies key numbers and time codes of clips against the camera and sound reports
Film editor syncs sound and picture by time code and checks sync
Film editor logs discrepancies and asks the set to clarify them
Film editor checks time codes in the edit list before conform and delivery

tasks.design: The camera assistant and sound recordist fill digital camera and sound reports on set with about the effort of the paper sheets. At ingest a script reads each clip's time code, reel and camera from the file metadata and compares them with the reports, listing only mismatches. Picture and sound are synced by time code, with the editor checking the clips the editing software marks as uncertain. Before conform, a check script compares the edit list's time codes with the source clips. Fixed rules only; no model is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Time codes were checked by eye against paper reports and copied into spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital camera and sound reports and file metadata that scripts can compare.
tasks.still_hard: Material shot without proper time code.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a clip is in sync by the numbers but not by the lips.
tasks.altitude: Most checking goes; judging sync stays with the editor.

reach.learn: Whether digital reports cut questions from the cutting room.

evidence.claim: Editing software matches clip transcripts to the script and cuts multicam to the active speaker.
File metadata and digital reports can be compared by script; no model is needed.

assumptions: Boundary: checking and syncing material from ingest to conform; editing is outside.
Input contract for s3: digital camera and sound reports filled on set by the camera assistant and sound recordist (s1), on about 80% of shoots; paper reports are typed; s3 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: time code recorded in camera and sound files; material without time code is synced by hand.
Receiving media keeps its full time; crew time is outside the editor's savings.
unknowns: Share of shoots with digital reports.

already_counted.description: Film editor checks mismatches and uncertain syncs the scripts list.

incremental.description: Film editor maintains the ingest and edit-list check scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: shoots with paper reports and mixed time code (s3 60, s4 70) (34.2); high: digital reports on about 80% of shoots and synced time code (55.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Shape the story in the timeline, manipulate plot, score, sound and graphics into a continuous whole, prepare turnovers for audio, music and effects departments, integrate their work and discuss changes with the director.

steps.what: Film editor manipulates plot and pacing in the timeline to make the parts into a continuous whole
Film editor places temp score, sound and graphics
Film editor prepares turnover files for the audio, music and effects departments
Film editor checks each turnover before it goes: the right cut version, and the change list and reference file match the timeline
Film editor delivers the checked turnovers to the audio, music and effects departments
Film editor reviews and integrates the departments' deliveries
Film editor works closely with the director and departments on changes

tasks.design: Shaping the story and the temp mix stay fully with the editor. Turnovers for sound, music and effects are exported with presets agreed once with each department, so each change list and reference file follows the same naming and format. Integrating deliveries uses the same agreed formats.

approvals.approved_version: Each turnover with its cut version, change list and reference file exactly as checked by the editor in s3b, delivered once to the named department; any recut needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Each turnover was set up by hand per department and per change.
tasks.enabler_now: Export presets in editing software agreed with departments.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping departments in step when the cut changes late.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling the rhythm a scene needs.

reach.learn: Whether standard turnovers cut rework after late changes.

evidence.claim: An editing tool's script matching yields a rough cut, not a finished edit.
No AI Act high-risk area applies to editing.

assumptions: Boundary: assembling the whole from picture, sound, music and effects; final mix and grade are other departments' work.
Input contract for s3: export presets agreed with each department at the start of the production.
Story work, temp mix and talks keep their full time.
research_questions: Do departments ask fewer questions about turnovers?

incremental.description: Film editor agrees export presets with each department.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small productions with one sound editor and few turnovers (s3 80) (3.6); high: series with many turnovers (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss the effect with the director, program computerized graphic effects and recurring titles, render and check them, and revise after feedback.

steps.what: Film editor discusses the graphic or effect with the director
Film editor programs the computerized graphic effects and titles
Film editor renders and checks the effects
Film editor revises the effects after feedback

tasks.design: Creative effects stay hand-built. Recurring graphics such as name titles and lower thirds come from templates filled from a data sheet of names and roles, and renders run in a background queue while the editor works on. Any realistic synthetic image of real people or events is labelled as the AI Act requires.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each title was typed and positioned by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Graphic templates driven by data sheets and background render queues.
tasks.human_edge: Designing a graphic that fits the film's look.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; recurring graphics take less time.

reach.learn: Whether name title errors fall when titles come from the list.

evidence.claim: AI-altered images or video that resemble real people or events must be disclosed as deep fakes.
Tool providers must mark synthetic output machine-readably by 2 December 2026 for systems already on the market.

assumptions: Boundary: building graphics and effects in the edit; high-end visual effects are another department's work.
Input contract for s2: a data sheet of names and roles kept by the production coordinator; about a quarter of graphics are recurring titles.
Briefs and revisions keep their full time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly bespoke effects with few name titles (s2 95) (4.0); high: documentaries and series with many name titles (9.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study scripts to become familiar with production concepts and requirements, break them down into scenes and requirements, and discuss the concept with the director and producer.

steps.what: Film editor studies the script to become familiar with the production concept
Film editor notes scenes, characters and editing requirements

loop.output: A list of scenes with number, location, characters and notes on effects, music or graphics mentioned.
loop.check: Every scene must quote its scene heading and page, or it is marked. The editor checks each scene's characters and mentioned effects, music and graphics against its page, and adds their own requirements.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scene headings are regular, but effects and music cues are buried in action lines.

steps.what: Film editor discusses the concept and requirements with the director and producer

tasks.design: Reading the script and the talks stay with the editor. A bounded step extracts a scene list with headings, pages, characters and mentioned effects, music and graphics, which the editor completes with their own notes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scene breakdowns were typed by hand from the script.
tasks.enabler_now: Models that extract structured lists from scripts with page references.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding the tone the director wants.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in the script where the film will need to breathe.

reach.learn: Whether a scene list from the script speeds up bin set-up.

evidence.claim: An editing tool matches clip transcripts to the script.
Language models can list scenes and cues from a script with page references.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing from the script; editing is outside.
Input contract for s2: the script as a text file in a standard screenplay layout; unpublished scripts stay within the production's own tools.
Reading and talks keep their full time.
unknowns: How often scripts change during the shoot.
research_questions: Is the breakdown used later in the edit?

already_counted.description: Film editor checks and completes the extracted scene list.

incremental.description: Film editor reruns the breakdown for new script versions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short scripts where the extraction saves little (s2 85) (3.5); high: long series scripts with many scenes (9.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
